questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, '**a nasal vaccine**' should be used instead of '**a nose-based vaccine**'.
 
• In the given sentence the **adjective** of '**nose**' that is '**nasal**' should be used. To modify the word '**vaccine**' we have to use the adjective '**nasal**'.
 
• The word '**nasal**' means 'of or for the nose'. (नाक का या नाक के लिए, नासिका-संबंधी)

• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 2.****
 

Correct Sentence:__** *India has identified **a nasal-based vaccine** against Covid-19 that could be a 'game-changer'.*

• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।

• दिए गए वाक्य में '**nasal**' अर्थात 'nose' के **Adjective** का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए। '**vaccine**' शब्द को **modify** करने के लिए हमें '**nasal**' के **adjective** का प्रयोग करना होगा।
 
• '**Nasal**' शब्द का अर्थ है 'नाक के लिए'।

• We need to follow the rule of parallelism as the subject '**Lavanya**' is common in the whole sentence, so the **same tense** shall be used to make it grammatically correct.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. As a result, he had a debt of 500 million US dollars at the time of his death.

B. Unfortunately, he began spending lavishly on anything he desired, not what he actually needed.

C. Michael Jackson, called the ‘King of Pop Music’, stayed at the top of his career for many years.

D. He was respected for his work culture; he would spend long nights at the studio to fix a note correctly in a song.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**CDBA**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Sentence C will be the first sentence because it is talking about Michael Jackson and this is an introductory sentence.
 
• Sentence D will be the next sentence because it further explains the kind of work he used to do the exertion he used to put in his songs.
 
• Sentence B will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence.
 
• Lastly, Sentence A will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• C: Michael Jackson, called the ‘King of Pop Music’, stayed at the top of his career for many years.
 
• D: He was respected for his work culture; he would spend long nights at the studio to fix a note correctly in a song.
 
• B: Unfortunately, he began spending lavishly on anything he desired, not what he actually needed.
 
• A: As a result, he had a debt of 500 million US dollars at the time of his death.

 
 
 

Correct Sequence:__ *Michael Jackson, called the ‘King of Pop Music’, stayed at the top of his career for many years. He was respected for his work culture; he would spend long nights at the studio to fix a note correctly in a song. Unfortunately, he began spending lavishly on anything he desired, not what he actually needed. As a result, he had a debt of 500 million US dollars at the time of his death.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Sai Kumari gave Akhila a bouquet of lilies on her birthday.

options.text: Akhila was gave a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.
Akhila is given a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.
Akhila gave a bouquet of lilies on her birthday to Sai Kumari.
Akhila was given a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Akhila was given a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'Sai Kumari'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'Akhila'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'gave' will be changed into 'was given'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.

 ​

Correct Sentence:__* Akhila was given a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** 

__
 
• ​दिया गया वाक्य Active Voice में है। दिए गए प्रश्न के अनुसार हमें इसे Passive Voice में बदलना है।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य की संरचना इस प्रकार है:
 
 
• Subject + V2+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• उदाहरण:
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• दिए गए वाक्य का विषय 'Sai Kumari' है।​
 
• दिए गए वाक्य का object 'Akhila' है।
 
• Object के स्थान पर Subject रखा जाएगा और Subject के स्थान पर Object रखा जाएगा।
 
• 'gave' को 'was given' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
 
• अंत में, 'by' preposition जोड़ा जाएगा।
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Humans work because they have to; they play because they want to.

B. The most useful definitions are those that clarify the relationship of sports to play, games and contests.

C. “Play,” wrote the German theorist Carl Diem, “is purposeless activity, for its own sake, the opposite of work.”

D. Sports are part of every culture, past and present, but each culture has its own definition of sports.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DBCA'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Sentence D will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence explaining the sports.
 
• Sentence B will be the next sentence because it further explains the definition of sports.
 
• Sentence C will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence.
 
• Lastly, Sentence A will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• D: Sports are part of every culture, past and present, but each culture has its own definition of sports.
 
• B: The most useful definitions are those that clarify the relationship of sports to play, games and contests.
 
• C: “Play,” wrote the German theorist Carl Diem, “is purposeless activity, for its own sake, the opposite of work.”
 
• A: Humans work because they have to; they play because they want to.

 
 
 

Correct Sequence:__ *Sports are part of every culture, past and present, but each culture has its own definition of sports. The most useful definitions are those that clarify the relationship of sports to play, games and contests. “Play,” wrote the German theorist Carl Diem, “is purposeless activity, for its own sake, the opposite of work.” Humans work because they have to; they play because they want to.*
